prompt: Hi, we need to send a status update to Dana, our head of logistics. The drone inventory audit is live at the main warehouse. It's cutting stock-counting time from 3 days to about 4 hours per cycle. Huge win. But there's a problem: the drone's camera fails to read barcodes in low-light conditions. The main warehouse has poor lighting on the north side, and that's where 40% of our inventory is. We tested it last week, and the read failure rate there is 1 in 5. The lighting upgrade to fix this would cost $15k, and it's not in this quarter's budget. We're not asking Dana to approve the spend right now, just to be aware. We think we can work around it by scheduling drone flights during daylight hours, but that might delay some counts by 2 days. Also, we haven't figured out if the low-light issue affects the secondary warehouse, which has skylights. We'll check that next week. Dana should just read this and know the status, no action needed unless she wants to flag it to finance.

Need to update Priya, our CFO, on the ad-tier performance. Quick status, no decision needed. We launched the ad-supported tier 6 weeks ago. Current numbers: ad revenue is $0.02 per user-hour. That's below our initial projection of $0.03. The cost of serving ad-supported streams is $0.01 higher per user-hour than the premium tier. Why? More ad insertion logic, more bandwidth for the same video quality, and some extra telemetry. So the margin per user-hour is negative. We're recalculating the break-even point now. The original model assumed we'd need $0.025 per user-hour to break even. We're not there yet. Also, the ad fill rate is at 75%, which is lower than the 90% we planned for. We don't know if that's seasonal or a targeting issue. We're testing a few fixes. Priya should just be aware of these numbers. We'll send a more detailed analysis with a recommendation in 2 weeks. No action needed from her right now.

PR for the orders table index migration. Reviewer: Ravi. Files changed: 3. Migration file, a new index definition, and a config change. Line counts: +120, -15. The migration adds a composite index on (customer_id, created_at) to speed up order history queries. We ran the test suite: 120 tests passing, 2 new tests added for the index behavior. One thing not tested: index size on disk. We didn't check how much space the new index takes up on a production-sized table. Our staging table is only 1 million rows, but production has 50 million. The index could be large. I'm not sure if that's a problem for our disk budget. Also, we didn't check the migration time on a large table. It might lock the table for a while. The migration is using a standard ALTER TABLE, which in Postgres can take a lock. We're not sure if that's acceptable. Ravi should review the migration and decide if we need to test the index size or use a different migration strategy. The PR is ready for his review.

PR description for the flaky retry-logic fix in the payments webhook. Reviewer: Alex. Files changed: 2. The webhook handler and a test file. Line counts: +80, -40. The issue was that retries were firing too aggressively, causing duplicate charge attempts. We fixed the retry logic to use exponential backoff with jitter. Tests: 45 passing, 3 new tests. The new tests cover retry timing and duplicate prevention. One thing untested: out-of-order event delivery. That's when a later event arrives before an earlier one. Our fix doesn't handle that case, and we didn't write a test for it. We're not sure if the payment provider can send events out of order. We've seen it happen once in staging, but not in production. Alex should review the fix and decide if we need to handle out-of-order events in this PR or file a follow-up. Also, the retry backoff now goes from 1 second to 5 minutes over 5 attempts. That seems reasonable, but we haven't tested the behavior under high load. The PR is ready.

PR for adding a caching layer to the session-store service. Reviewer: Sam. Files changed: 4. The cache implementation, a config file, the service main file, and a test file. Line counts: +200, -30. We added an in-memory cache in front of the session store. Latency dropped from 120ms to 30ms on the read path, which is a 75% improvement. The write path is unchanged at 100ms. We ran the test suite: all existing tests pass, plus 5 new tests for cache hit/miss behavior. One thing untested: cache-eviction race condition. That's when two requests try to evict and repopulate the same key at the same time. We didn't write a test for that. We think the code handles it with a mutex, but we're not 100% sure. Sam should review the eviction logic and decide if we need a test for the race condition or if the mutex is sufficient. Also, the cache size is set to 10,000 entries. We don't know if that's enough for peak traffic. We'll monitor. The PR is ready for review.

PR for upgrading the TLS library across all services. Reviewer: the security lead, Jordan. Files changed: 12. All service configs and the shared TLS setup. Line counts: +60, -50. We upgraded from TLS 1.2 to TLS 1.3 across all 12 services. Handshake time improved from 40ms to 25ms on average. That's a 37% reduction. We ran the full test suite: 230 tests passing, 0 new tests. The change is mostly config. One question for Jordan: there's a cipher suite deprecation. The old library supports TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA, but the new library marks it as deprecated. We didn't deprecate it in our config, so it's still enabled. We're not sure if we should remove it now or keep it for backward compatibility with older clients. Jordan should decide if we can drop that cipher suite or if we need to keep it for a while. Also, we didn't test the handshake under heavy load, but the numbers look good. The PR is ready for Jordan's review.

PR for adding a circuit breaker to the downstream inventory API. Reviewer: Chris. Files changed: 3. The circuit breaker class, the API client, and a test file. Line counts: +150, -20. The inventory API has been flaky, with error rates spiking to 15% during peak hours. We added a circuit breaker that opens after 5 consecutive failures and stays open for 30 seconds. During the open state, we return a cached response. Error rate dropped to 2% in our tests. We ran the test suite: 180 tests passing, 4 new tests for the circuit breaker. One thing untested: slow-response case. That's when the API responds slowly but doesn't error out. Our circuit breaker doesn't handle that. It only counts failures, not timeouts. We didn't test or implement a timeout-based trip. Chris should review and decide if we need to add a timeout-based circuit breaker in this PR or if the failure-based one is enough for now. Also, the cached response is from 5 minutes ago, which might be stale. We're not sure if that's acceptable. The PR is ready.

PR for swapping the message-broker client library in the order-events service. Reviewer: Taylor. Files changed: 5. The producer, the consumer, the config, and two test files. Line counts: +250, -180. We swapped from the old client to the new one. Throughput improved from 5,000 messages/second to 8,000 messages/second on the producer side. Consumer side is similar. We ran the test suite: 150 tests passing, 6 new tests for the new client's API. One thing untested: broker-restart case. That's when the broker goes down and comes back up. The new client should reconnect automatically, but we didn't test that. We're not sure if the reconnection logic works correctly with our config. Taylor should review the reconnection code and decide if we need to test the broker-restart case or if the client library's default behavior is sufficient. Also, we didn't test the behavior when the broker is down for more than 60 seconds. Our current config has a 30-second reconnect timeout. The PR is ready for review.

PR for lazy-loading modules to cut the mobile app's startup time. Reviewer: Morgan, our mobile lead. Files changed: 6. The app entry point, a module loader, and four feature modules. Line counts: +180, -90. We moved the analytics, chat, and settings modules to lazy load. Startup time dropped from 3.5 seconds to 2.1 seconds on a mid-range device. That's a 40% improvement. We tested on two devices: a Pixel 7 and a Samsung A13. The Pixel 7 went from 3.2s to 1.9s, the A13 from 4.1s to 2.6s. We ran the test suite: 90 tests passing, 3 new tests for the lazy loader. One thing untested: low-memory-device case. We didn't test on a device with less than 2GB of RAM. The lazy loading might cause memory pressure when modules are loaded on demand. Morgan should review the loading strategy and decide if we need to test on a low-memory device or if the current approach is safe. Also, we're not sure if the chat module loads fast enough when the user opens it. The PR is ready.

PR for adding a read replica path for the reporting dashboard. Reviewer: the on-call lead, Pat. Files changed: 4. The database config, a new query router, the dashboard service, and a test file. Line counts: +140, -25. We added a read replica for the dashboard's heavy queries. The dashboard's main query latency dropped from 800ms to 150ms on the replica. That's an 81% improvement. We ran the test suite: 110 tests passing, 2 new tests for the read/write split. One question for Pat: we need to decide on replica-lag alerting. We set up a simple alert if the replica lags more than 5 seconds, but we're not sure if that's the right threshold. The dashboard can tolerate some lag, but we don't know how much. Pat should decide on the alerting threshold and if we need a more sophisticated lag detection. Also, we didn't test the failover behavior if the replica goes down. The query router should fall back to the primary, but we didn't test that. The PR is ready for Pat's review.
